abstract: For $(x,y)\in\mathbb{R}^2$ and $Q\ge 1$, set $F_Q(x,y)=Q\min_{1\le q\le Q}\lVert qx\rVert\lVert qy\rVert$, where $q$ ranges over positive integers and $\lVert\cdot\rVert$ denotes distance to the nearest integer. The set on which the uniform Littlewood constant $L=\limsup_{Q\to\infty}F_Q$ is positive has full Hausdorff dimension. We prove that for every fixed $c>0$ the superlevel set $\{L\ge c\}$ has Hausdorff dimension strictly less than two. More precisely, the Lebesgue measure of $\{(x,y)\in[0,1]^2:F_Q(x,y)\ge c\}$ is $O_c(Q^{-\kappa(c)})$ for some $\kappa(c)>0$ and all $Q\ge 2$. The proof combines large deviations for one diagonal action on the space of unimodular lattices with effective equidistribution of expanding horospheres for another.
hook: The set of points with uniformly large Littlewood constant has Hausdorff dimension strictly below two.
summary: Littlewood's conjecture concerns how well two numbers can be approximated by fractions with a shared denominator. The author shows the set where a uniform version of this constant stays at least c has dimension below two, with its measure at scale Q shrinking like a power of Q. The proof joins large deviations for one diagonal flow on lattices with equidistribution of expanding horospheres for another. It does not resolve the conjecture itself.
title: Dimension drop for superlevel sets of the uniform Littlewood constant
